clue.text: A conquering female marshal eads her attack

indicators.note: to marshal troops is to arrange them in a new order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the published text drops the first letter of 'leads', so the fodder as meant is leads her attack

explanation.surface: A victorious woman general leads her troops into an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published reads 'eads', a slip for 'leads'. 'marshal' rearranges LEADS HER ATTACK. Kate Hardcastle is the heroine of Goldsmith's She Stoops to Conquer.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith's heroine pretends to be a barmaid, stooping to win her suitor, so she is the woman of the play's title who conquers.

clue.text: Spreading the gospel, of Mark for example, helpfully at last in translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into new forms, here signalling the letters are rearranged
at last picks out only the final letter of the word helpfully

explanation.surface: Translating a Gospel such as Mark's is a helpful way to spread the Christian message.
explanation.walkthrough: MARK, EG and Y (the last letter of 'helpfully') are rearranged. Kerygma is the theologians' term for the apostolic proclamation of the gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek-derived theological term means preaching or proclamation of the Christian message.

clue.text: He wrote books about Sam, a famous batsman given an award

parts.note: a Tony is an American award for theatre
Don Bradman, the great Australian cricketer

explanation.surface: A biographer writes about a cricketing hero who has received an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Donald Bradman was the greatest batsman in cricket history. Tony Bradman is a British children's author.
explanation.definitionFit: This British children's writer produced picture books featuring a young character named Sam, among many series.

clue.text: Artist responsible for many large-scale pointillist works

definitions.text: Artist responsible for many large-scale pointillist works

parts.words: Artist responsible for many large-scale pointillist works
parts.note: the 'pointillist works' are not Seurat-style dabs but a modern British artist's famous grids of coloured spots, the spot paintings

explanation.definitionFit: Damien's spot paintings are big canvases covered in regularly spaced dots, a joking kind of pointillism.

clue.text: He worked on operas with Diana, a famous singer in Italy

parts.note: Diana Ross, the American singer
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A composer collaborated on operas with a celebrated diva in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer of The Barber of Seville wrote dozens of operas.

clue.text: French form of cure almost cuts short lives

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a curé is the French form of a parish priest, that is, a cleric
hews means cuts, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A French remedy nearly shortens people's lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CLERIC to CLERI. A clerihew is a four-line comic verse about a famous person, invented by Edmund Clerihew Bentley.
explanation.definitionFit: These comic quatrains are tiny biographies of their subjects, so each is a brief life in verse.

clue.text: Vicious name for Caesar in satirical comedy

definitions.meaning: ... Vicious was the bass player of the Sex Pistols; this is his first name

definitions.text: name for Caesar in satirical comedy
definitions.meaning: ... Caesar was an American comedian of television sketch satire; this is his first name

explanation.surface: A cruel nickname for a Roman ruler appears in a satirical play.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the punk Vicious and the comedian Caesar had this short first name.

clue.text: A sailor in a French composer's vocal composition

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Jean-Baptiste Lully, composer at the court of Louis XIV
an AB is an able seaman, so a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman features in a song by a French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle song sung to soothe a child is a short piece for the voice.

clue.text: An English king in Ireland

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An English monarch is staying in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the poetic old name for the Emerald Isle.

clue.text: Saints, with objective unknown, in slowing down Rudolf

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces inside the musical abbreviation

parts.note: rall., short for rallentando, is the musical direction to slow down
an end is an aim or objective
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: Saints with no clear goal are making slow progress in Rudolf's life.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf Rassendyll is the Englishman who impersonates the king in Anthony Hope's The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope's hero's full name is Rudolf Rassendyll, so the first name points to the surname.

clue.text: United try to be sure with note on Italian playmaker

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
to have a go is to try
'you bet' means certainly, to be sure
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A football team strives for certainty, its hopes resting on an Italian midfield playmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playmaker' looks like football but means a maker of plays: Ugo Betti was an Italian dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Betti was an Italian dramatist, so literally a maker of plays.

clue.text: Is divine sympathy expressed in part of the Bible?

parts.note: divine in the sense of superb is A1, written AI
ah is a sound expressing sympathy

explanation.surface: A question about whether God's compassion is shown in some book of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks theological but is slang for excellent, A1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: This prophetic book is one of the books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Stanley who falls in love with a demonstrator met in London, in an Edwardian novel

definitions.text: Stanley who falls in love with a demonstrator met in London, in an Edwardian novel

parts.words: Stanley who falls in love with a demonstrator met in London, in an Edwardian novel
parts.note: describes the heroine of H. G. Wells's 1909 novel, a young woman surnamed Stanley who falls for Capes, the demonstrator in her biology classes in London

explanation.definitionFit: Wells's heroine, whose name is also the novel's title, is a New Woman who falls for her science demonstrator.

clue.text: Parsons produced this result of a church service

definitions.meaning: Tony Parsons wrote a novel with this title, a sequel to Man and Boy
a wedding ceremony ends with the couple declared husband and spouse

explanation.surface: Clergymen produced this outcome of a church ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage service makes a couple into husband and spouse, and Tony Parsons's novel bears the phrase as its title.

clue.text: "— is the only conversationalist who triumphs over time" (Harold Nicolson)

definitions.text: "— is the only conversationalist who triumphs over time" (Harold Nicolson)

parts.words: "— is the only conversationalist who triumphs over time" (Harold Nicolson)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: Nicolson praises the eighteenth-century talker whose remarks survive through Boswell's biography

explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson's talk lives on in Boswell's Life, so he outlasts time as a conversationalist.

clue.text: Negative responses — those voiced by hacks, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: hacks are hired or worn-out horses, and the sounds they make are neighs

explanation.surface: Journalists, it seems, are voicing their refusals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacks' wants to be journalists, but here they are horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes or answers of no are the opposite of ayes.

clue.text: Dodgy business is constant in a historical part of the Old Testament

indicators.note: in places the constant inside the book's abbreviation

parts.words: a historical part of the Old Testament
parts.note: Sam is the abbreviation for Samuel, one of the historical books
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Shady dealing is a recurring feature of an Old Testament history.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraudulent scheme or swindle is a shady piece of business.

clue.text: Goldsmith's instruments not included initially

parts.note: celli is a plural of cello

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of each of the words not and included

explanation.surface: A goldsmith's tools have not been included at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Benvenuto Cellini was the Renaissance Florentine goldsmith and sculptor; 'Goldsmith' also suggests Oliver Goldsmith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Renaissance artist was most famous for metalwork such as his golden salt cellar.

clue.text: Reportedly Holland never stirred a French writer

indicators.note: reportedly means the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Jools Holland, the British pianist and TV music presenter

indicators.note: stirred means the letters of never are mixed up

explanation.surface: It is said the Netherlands was never moved by a French author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holland' looks like the country, but it is Jools Holland, a British pianist and music TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea was a nineteenth-century French novelist.

clue.text: Mozart's house, quiet and antique

parts.note: Leo is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
antique means old

explanation.surface: Mozart's home was peaceful and very old.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mozart meant is not Wolfgang but his father, the violinist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang's father, a violinist and composer, also bore the family surname.

clue.text: "I am tired out with his (.) depravity. I wish a milder word would do; I am -" (The Tenant of Wildfell Hall)

definitions.text: "I am tired out with his (.) depravity. I wish a milder word would do; I am -" (The Tenant of Wildfell Hall)

parts.words: "I am tired out with his (.) depravity. I wish a milder word would do; I am -" (The Tenant of Wildfell Hall)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: Helen Huntingdon, in Anne Bronte's novel, admits that she too is far from saintly

explanation.definitionFit: To say one is far from perfect, no heavenly being, is the idiom that completes Helen's confession.

clue.text: The End may come one day for this underused feature of Trafalgar Square

definitions.text: The End may come one day for this underused feature of Trafalgar Square

parts.words: The End may come one day for this underused feature of Trafalgar Square
parts.note: the Fourth stand in the square stood empty for years; 'The End' is a Heather Phillipson sculpture of whipped cream, cherry and drone shown on it, so it sounds like doom but names an artwork

explanation.walkthrough: The Fourth Plinth in Trafalgar Square, London, was empty for over 150 years and now shows rotating artworks.
explanation.definitionFit: The square's fourth statue base was long left without a statue, the base itself being the feature.

clue.text: Knitting wool with damn wise lady?

indicators.note: knitting works the material into new shapes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued, wise woman knits wool and swears.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: an elderly woman is thought wise.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly woman is traditionally imagined as full of wisdom, like the folk-tale crone.

clue.text: God, an original feature of the first book of Samuel

definitions.text: God, an original feature of the first book of Samuel

indicators.note: original in the sense of new and novel, so the letters of the words before it are made anew

explanation.surface: A deity makes a distinctive appearance early in Samuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Philistine god's statue falls before the Ark of the Covenant in 1 Samuel 5; the whole clue defines him and its first words supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine deity whose idol topples before the Ark appears in the fifth chapter of 1 Samuel.

clue.text: A famous expression of innocent hope — good start after Paddy has to depart

definitions.text: A famous expression of innocent hope

indicators.note: after places the start of good at the end

parts.note: a paddy and the pip are both a fit of bad temper
to pass on is to die, to depart

indicators.note: start picks out the opening letter of good

explanation.surface: Hope of a famous kind: a good start once an Irishman has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman but is a temper, a pip. Browning's lyric from Pippa Passes ends 'God's in His heaven / All's right with the world'.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning's innocent silk-weaver sings that all is right with the world, a famous lyric of trusting optimism.

clue.text: One description of Joey is mostly dim"

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: pale light is dim

explanation.surface: One way to describe a young kangaroo is as rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: John O'Hara's Pal Joey, later a musical, gives the word that describes Joey.
explanation.definitionFit: In the title of O'Hara's book and the Rodgers and Hart musical, Joey is described as a friend.

clue.text: I am Dean Martin, gentlemanly in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crooner introduces himself as Dean Martin, in a courteous sort of way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean Martin' looks like the singer, but the Dean is W. R. Inge, the 'Gloomy Dean' of St Paul's, speaking in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: William Ralph Inge was Dean of St Paul's, so he could say he is the Dean.

clue.text: The cockney squire's posh house by the location of Heathrow airport

parts.note: Heathrow lies in the London borough of Hillingdon
a hall is a grand country house

explanation.surface: A Londoner landowner's grand home lies next to Heathrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Surtees's novel is subtitled The Cockney Squire; its hero is the cockney grocer Jorrocks, who becomes a country squire.
explanation.definitionFit: R. S. Surtees's Jorrocks novel carries that subtitle, so the title stands for the book.
